I am 63 years old, and my bones tell me when the weather is about to turn. With just my wife and me on 10.1 mu, I cannot afford to waste labor or money. After 45 years, I know which plots drain well and which hold water. I keep 8 mu in my wheat-maize double crop — that rotation is reliable and feeds us. The remaining 2.1 mu stays in cotton, but I will not expand it; hand-picking cotton at my age is hard work, and I would rather sell grain than break my back.

For wheat, I will plant an improved winter wheat variety in October. I will rotary till first to break up the stubble and level the field. I will irrigate three times: before winter freeze, at jointing, and at grain filling. Two pesticide sprays — one herbicide early and one fungicide if the weather turns damp — is enough. I know this soil, so I will apply nitrogen carefully; too much makes the plants lodge, and at my age I cannot afford a bad stand.

For summer maize, I will plant a hybrid immediately after wheat harvest, no-tillage. The window between harvest and planting is only a few days, and no-tillage saves me time and fuel. Maize roots well into the wheat stubble. I will irrigate twice: once when the tassels are forming and once at grain filling. Two sprays will handle weeds and the occasional corn borer.

For cotton, I will plough deeply in spring because cotton roots need loose soil down deep. I will use an improved Bt variety. Cotton needs more potassium than grain crops, so I give it extra K. I will irrigate three times and spray four times — cotton always brings more insects. But I keep it to 2.1 mu because by harvest time in autumn, every jin of cotton passes through my hands.

I expect about 510 kg per mu from wheat, 590 kg per mu from maize, and 270 kg per mu of seed cotton. That is honest land, honestly farmed.

decision.reasoning_summary: With only two people in the household and at 63 years of age, I prioritize labor efficiency and reliable crops. The wheat-maize double crop on 8 mu is my core income and food security base, using no-tillage for maize to save time and rotary tillage for wheat to prepare a good seedbed. I limit cotton to 2.1 mu because it is labor-intensive to pick and manage, but the soil suits it and prices can be decent.
